name: Athaliah
charge: Destroying the seed royal of Judah; usurping the throne
summary: Ahab's daughter, married into Judah's line, saw her son Ahaziah dead at Jehu's hand and murdered all the seed royal to reign herself. One infant, Joash, was hidden in the house of the Lord for six years. In the seventh, Jehoiada the priest brought him out.
offense: When Ahaziah died, Athaliah rose against the royal seed and seized the kingdom. Jehosheba rescued Joash and hid him with his nurse, preserving a child from the destruction (2 Kings 11:1-3). Athaliah's possession of the throne rested upon violence against the house she should have protected. Her reign also belonged to the corruption of worship. Her sons had broken up God's house and devoted its things to Baalim (2 Chronicles 24:7). The seizure of the kingdom and misuse of holy possessions joined the same disregard for what had been entrusted to the royal house.
judgment: In the seventh year Jehoiada revealed the king's son, arranged his protection, and crowned him with the testimony. Athaliah heard the rejoicing and cried treason when she saw him standing in his place (2 Kings 11:4-14). The cry came from the ruler whose own position had been obtained by destroying the succession. Jehoiada ordered her taken outside rather than killed within the Lord's house. She was slain by the way leading to the king's house, and the people broke down Baal's house (2 Kings 11:15-18). The covenant was renewed, the people rejoiced, and the city was quiet. The hidden child outlasted the reign that had sought to erase him.

verses.text: And when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons which were slain; and they hid him, even him and his nurse, in the bedchamber from Athaliah, so that he was not slain.
And he was with her hid in the house of the Lord six years. And Athaliah did reign over the land.
And when Athaliah heard the noise of the guard and of the people, she came to the people into the temple of the Lord.

And when she looked, behold, the king stood by a pillar, as the manner was, and the princes and the trumpeters by the king, and all the people of the land rejoiced, and blew with trumpets: and Athaliah rent her clothes, and cried, Treason, Treason.

But Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of the hundreds, the officers of the host, and said unto them, Have her forth without the ranges: and him that followeth her kill with the sword. For the priest had said, Let her not be slain in the house of the Lord.
And they laid hands on her; and she went by the way by the which the horses came into the king’s house: and there was she slain.
But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,) hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not.
And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land.
Now when Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people into the house of the Lord:

And she looked, and, behold, the king stood at his pillar at the entering in, and the princes and the trumpets by the king: and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded with trumpets, also the singers with instruments of musick, and such as taught to sing praise. Then Athaliah rent her clothes, and said, Treason, Treason.

Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds that were set over the host, and said unto them, Have her forth of the ranges: and whoso followeth her, let him be slain with the sword. For the priest said, Slay her not in the house of the Lord.
So they laid hands on her; and when she was come to the entering of the horse gate by the king’s house, they slew her there.
For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God; and also all the dedicated things of the house of the Lord did they bestow upon Baalim.
Two and twenty years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the Lord, as did the house of Ahab: for he was the son in law of the house of Ahab.

entries.commentary: When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw her son was dead, she moved to destroy all the royal seed so she could seize the throne. Jehosheba, sister of Ahaziah, took the infant Joash and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being slain, hiding him in the house of the Most High for six years while Athaliah reigned. The rightful king was preserved and concealed the entire time the usurper sat on the throne.

In the seventh year Jehoiada the priest brought the captains together, took an oath of them in the house of the Most High, and showed them the king's son. He commanded them how to guard the king by watches and companies so that the house would not be broken down. The guard was to compass the king round about, every man with his weapon in his hand, and to stay with him as he went out and came in. -
Every man stood armed around the king, and any who came within the ranges was to be slain.

The captains did according to all that Jehoiada commanded, taking their men to the priest. Jehoiada gave the captains King David's spears and shields that were in the temple, and the guard stood every man with his weapons in hand around the king. Then he brought forth the king's son, put the crown upon him, gave him the testimony, anointed him, and the people clapped their hands and said, God save the king. The weapons they carried then were physical; today the weapon of Israel is the scriptures.

Athaliah heard the noise of the guard and the people and came into the temple, and saw the king standing by a pillar as the manner was. She rent her clothes and cried, Treason, treason, but Jehoiada commanded the captains to have her forth outside the ranges. She was not to be slain in the house of the Most High, so they took her out by the way the horses came into the king's house and slew her there.

Jehoiada made a covenant between the Most High, the king, and the people, that they should be the Lord's people. All the people went to the house of Baal, broke down its altars and images, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. Joash was brought to the throne, the people rejoiced, the city was quiet, and he was seven years old when he began to reign. This same covenant is what happens today: as a person wakes up, repents, keeps the commandments, and comes out of idolatry, they again become the Lord's people.

The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, king in his stead, for the band of Arabians had slain all the elder sons. Ahaziah was forty and two years old when he began to reign and reigned one year in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri. He walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly, and the house of Ahab were his counsellors after his father died, to his destruction. This is a warning against being ruled by the wrong counsel: instead of going to the priests and the judges, he went to his mother, and she counselled him into ruin. A woman with a grudge can rule a kingdom through her son, and that is what Athaliah did.

Ahaziah walked after their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, where Jehoram was wounded. He went down to see the wounded Jehoram at Jezreel, and the destruction of Ahaziah was of the Most High, for by going he came into the path of Jehu, whom the Most High had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. That same Jehu who killed the seventy sons of Ahab found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brethren and slew them, then sought and caught Ahaziah, who was hid in Samaria. They buried Ahaziah for the sake of Jehoshaphat his forefather who sought the Most High with all his heart; but the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep the kingdom, so the wicked king was cut off by the same hand the Most High anointed to avenge Israel.

When Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah, killing the king's sons. But Jehoshabeath the daughter of king Jehoram, wife of Jehoiada the priest and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, hiding him and his nurse in a bedchamber. She hid the child in the house of God six years while Athaliah reigned over the land, showing that Athaliah was ruling in the position of the son she had lost. Athaliah did not carry out this slaughter alone; she had weak men helping her run over everything, which is how she seized and held the throne.

In the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the captains of hundreds into covenant with him, and they gathered the Levites and the chief of the fathers out of all the cities of Judah to Jerusalem. The congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God, and Jehoiada declared that the king's son should reign, as the Most High had said of the sons of David. He set his plan: a third part of the priests and Levites to keep the doors, a third at the king's house, and a third at the gate of the foundation, with all the people in the courts. None but the priests and ministering Levites were to enter the house of the Most High, and the Levites were to compass the king round about, every man with his weapon, and put to death any who forced their way in.

The Levites and all Judah did according to all Jehoiada commanded, each man keeping his company, for Jehoiada did not dismiss the courses of the Levites but kept them at their work with security added for the king. Jehoiada delivered to the captains the spears and shields that had been king David's, kept in the house of God, and set every man with his weapon from one side of the temple to the other, round about the king. They brought out the king's son, put the crown upon him, gave him the testimony, and made him king, and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, God save the king. This was done by the proper custom: a priest anoints the king, as Samuel the priest anointed Saul and then David; so Jehoiada the priest anointed Joash.

When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came into the house of the Most High and saw the king standing at his pillar with the princes, trumpets, and singers rejoicing. She rent her clothes and cried, Treason, treason, but her cry came too late, for the covenant was already made and the true king was crowned. Jehoiada commanded the captains to have her forth from the ranges and to slay any that followed her, but not to slay her in the house of the Most High. They laid hands on her, brought her to the entering of the horse gate by the king's house, and slew her there, ending the reign of the woman who had killed the seed royal.

Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, all the people, and the king, that they should be the Most High's people, and the people went to the house of Baal, broke it down, brake its altars and images, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal. Jehoiada appointed the officers of the house of the Most High by the hand of the priests and Levites whom David had distributed, to offer burnt offerings with rejoicing and singing as ordained by David. He set the porters at the gates so that none unclean in anything should enter, then brought the king down and set him upon the throne of the kingdom, and the people rejoiced and the city was quiet. Before a king is set in his position he is under tutors and governors; young Joash was king in rank, yet he was still a learner under Jehoiada, for even kings had to be taught. Athaliah had no place ruling Israel; being the king's mother did not make her the ruler. -

Joash was seven years old when he began to reign and reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba. Joash did that which was right in the sight of the Most High all the days of Jehoiada the priest, because that is what he was taught. He had seen the wicked men of Israel try to kill him, so he followed the man who showed him the ropes; Jehoiada taught him how to be a righteous king and keep the commandments. A king had a job to do and could not simply sit back; he had a kingdom to watch over, and he had the priests there to help him do it.

Joash was minded to repair the house of the Most High and gathered the priests and Levites, telling them to go to the cities of Judah and gather money of all Israel to repair the house from year to year, and to hasten the matter. The Levites did not hasten it, so the king called Jehoiada the chief and asked why he had not required of the Levites the collection appointed by Moses for the tabernacle of witness. Money was needed because Israel did not let the workmen labor for nothing; when men did the jobs they were paid, for the workman is worthy of his hire, and we dealt righteously with our people. The sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God and bestowed all its dedicated things upon Baalim, which is why so much repair was needed.

At the king's commandment they made a chest and set it at the gate of the house of the Most High, and made a proclamation to bring in the collection Moses laid upon Israel in the wilderness, and the princes and people rejoiced and cast in until they made an end. Day by day the king's scribe and the high priest's officer emptied the chest and gathered money in abundance, and the king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work, hiring masons, carpenters, and workers of iron and brass. Money was a defense here because it paid the skilled brothers who got the temple work done; we must deal righteously with our people today, treating a brother's business as a place to help the family and the body. Not everyone was given the same task; masons, carpenters, and metalworkers each had their charge, and every man had to listen to a manager, for business requires order and submission to authority. The workmen perfected the work and set the house of God in its state, then brought the rest of the money to make vessels of gold and silver to minister and offer with, and they offered burnt offerings continually all the days of Jehoiada. -

Jehoiada waxed old and was full of days and died, being a hundred and thirty years old at his death. They buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel both toward the Most High and toward his house. That a priest was buried among the kings shows how much respect and diligence this man had earned; his faithfulness set him alongside the rulers of the land.

After the death of Jehoiada the princes of Judah came and made obeisance to the king, and the king hearkened to them. They left the house of the Most High and served groves and idols, and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for their trespass. The Most High sent prophets to bring them again unto Him, and they testified against them, but the people would not give ear. As soon as Jehoiada died, Israel went off again, because the king was weak and started listening to those who served other gods; this teaches the lesson that lust drives Israel to idolatry, and that the Most High will always send prophets to warn them.

The spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, who stood above the people and asked why they transgressed the commandments so that they could not prosper, telling them that because they had forsaken the Most High, He had also forsaken them. They conspired against Zechariah and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king, in the court of the house of the Most High. When the prophet came to correct the king, the king had him killed for telling him the truth; this is the same spirit our people show when a laborer brings the medicine and is met with violence. As Zechariah died he said, The Most High look upon it and require it. He prayed for vengeance on his murderer, and this is scripture; it is right to pray for the downfall of enemies who do much wickedness, even while we pray for the recovery and repentance of our own people. -

At the end of the year the host of Syria came up against Joash, destroyed the princes of the people, and sent the spoil to the king of Damascus. The Syrians came with a small company, yet the Most High delivered a very great host of Judah into their hand, because Judah had forsaken the Most High God of their fathers; so judgment was executed on Joash for killing Zechariah. They left Joash in great diseases, and his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada and slew him on his bed, and he was buried in the city of David but not in the sepulchres of the kings. Joash began by doing right under Jehoiada's guidance, repairing the house and clearing out the idols, but none of that was remembered in the end because of the wickedness he turned to after being warned. Amaziah his son reigned in his stead; the fuller record of Joash is written in the story of the book of the kings. -

Elisha warns the Shunammite woman whose son he restored to flee the coming seven year famine, and she sojourns in the land of the Philistines. When she returns to appeal to the king for her house and land, Gehazi is at that moment telling the king how Elisha restored a dead body to life. The timing is of the Most High, so the king restores all that was hers and the fruits of the field from the day she left.

Ben-hadad king of Syria, sick, sends Hazael to inquire of Elisha whether he will recover, for the word of a prophet, also called a seer, was precious in those days. Elisha tells Hazael the king may recover but the Most High has shown that he shall surely die, then weeps because he sees the evil Hazael will do to Israel: burning strongholds, slaying young men, and ripping up women with child. Elisha tells Hazael he will be king over Syria, revealing that leadership can discern spirits at work in a man that the man does not see in himself. Hazael returns and smothers the king with a wet cloth and reigns in his place.

Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife. He does evil in the sight of the Most High, yet Judah is not destroyed for David his servant's sake, according to the promise.

In Jehoram's days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah and makes a king over itself, breaking the subjection Edom had been under from the days of David and Solomon. This revolt fulfills the word spoken to Esau, that when he gained the dominion he would break the yoke from off his neck, a pattern reaching to Edom's later rise. Jehoram sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place. -

Ahaziah son of Jehoram begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the house of Ahab, being the son-in-law of that house, a picture of the generational curse passed from father to son. He goes with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria, and the Syrians wound Jehoram at Ramah. Jehoram returns to Jezreel to be healed, and Ahaziah goes down to see him, setting the stage for both kings to meet Jehu's judgment.

lawsResolved.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
Civil leaders and authorities are to be men not women.
Government officers that engage in conspiracy, treachery and murder are to be put to death.
Rebellion and insurrection against the government is punishable by death.
You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
